title: A Blow for a Blow
blurb: You have a year-old promise, a green axe, and four days to find the man who will use it on you.

brief.premise: A green man rode into the New Year feast, took a blow, picked up his own head and named the day of the return blow. The year is up and the debt is yours.
brief.setting: the winter country north of Camelot: fen, pinewood and a frozen dale
brief.storyline: ride to the Green Chapel by way of a lord's roof, and find out what a promise costs when nobody is watching
brief.protagonist: Sir Gawain, who accepted the blow so that the king would not have to
brief.avoid: battles, monsters that can be fought, anything that rewards violence

lore.title: A Blow for a Blow
lore.premise: The green man let a knight take his head off at the New Year feast, then picked it up and asked for the return blow in a twelvemonth. Nobody at that table thought he would come back for it. The twelvemonth is up.
lore.era: the turning of the year, and the twelfth winter of the Round Table

235836158.name: The Winter Waste
235836158.blurb: Pinewood and frozen fen, going north until it stops being anybody's.
235836158.culture: Fowlers and ferrymen who have learned not to be out after dark.
lore: Nothing between the fen and the fells has been consecrated in living memory.
The lords out here keep Christmas because the alternative is not keeping it.
ambient: The frost has not come off the north side of anything today.
Your breath is going ahead of you in the cold.
There is holly in the hedge, and a great deal of it.

2510667258.name: The King's Hundred
2510667258.blurb: Cropped meadow and cart-track, kept clear because the court rides through it.
2510667258.culture: Bondsmen who owe the hall service and get the road mended for it.
lore: Everything within a day of the hall is somebody's to answer for.
ambient: The verges have been cut back this side of the year.
Somebody has swept the frost off this stretch of the track.

2557665069.name: Helm Hundred
2557665069.blurb: Helm Hundred is highland country, and keeps to itself.
ambient: The wind moves across the highland.
The frost has not come off the north side of anything today.
Somewhere behind you a bird goes up out of the reeds, and nothing follows it.
Your breath is going ahead of you in the cold.
There is holly in the hedge, and a great deal of it.
The track has been ridden this winter, but not lately.

347348444.name: Holm Ferry
347348444.description: Three roofs, a quay of rammed stone, and more boats than there are people to row them. The channel is the only way north that is not fen.

npcs.name: Hodierne the ferryman
npcs.appearance: Standing in the boat rather than beside it, out of long habit.
npcs.persona: Talks about the water the way other people talk about a relative they cannot get rid of.
knows: The mooring iron went into the reeds north of the quay and she has not got it back.
There is a mound out east past the pines that the fowlers will not walk over.
Whatever is out there rings like a smith at first light and is not a smith.

npcs.name: Alisoun the netmaker
npcs.appearance: Mending, with the work hooked over one bare toe.
npcs.persona: Cheerfully certain that everybody who goes north is a fool, present company included.
knows: Two riders went north at Martinmas and one horse came back.
The lord out in the pines pays in venison and pays well.

hooks: The ferry's mooring iron is somewhere in the reeds and the boats are tied to a stake.

3199628140.name: Camelot
3199628140.description: A curtain wall on cropped meadow, hung with more holly than it has any use for. The court is keeping Christmas very loudly, and has been for eleven days.

npcs.name: Arthur
npcs.appearance: Younger than the songs have him, and refusing to sit down while there is a thing unsettled in his hall.
npcs.persona: Courteous to the point of cruelty to himself. Will not say the word that would keep you here.
knows: The green axe is still in the keep. Nobody has wanted to move it.
There is a lord's roof out in the waste that keeps the feast: Hautdesert.
He would go himself. That is precisely the trouble.

npcs.name: Sir Kay
npcs.appearance: Standing in the gateway out of the wind, with a list nobody asked him for.
npcs.persona: Rude as a form of affection. Has already had your horse shod.
knows: The road north runs to Holm Ferry and then out into the fen.
Hautdesert is the last roof before the waste; after that there is nothing to knock on.
He does not believe in the Green Chapel and has said so at length.

npcs.name: Bishop Baldwin
npcs.appearance: Ink to the knuckle, and a cloak worn thin across the shoulders.
npcs.persona: Kind, brisk, and entirely certain the vow must be kept.
knows: A promise made in a hall is still a promise made.
The five joys, the five wounds, the five virtues: the shield is an argument, not a decoration.

npcs.name: Elyan the harper
npcs.appearance: Fingers wrapped against the cold, tuning something that is already in tune.
npcs.persona: Would very much like to sing the verse he has been asked not to sing.
knows: There is a verse about the green man that the queen has forbidden at table.
In the verse the knight does not come home.

hooks: The axe the green man left has been hanging in the keep for a twelvemonth and nobody will touch it.
The court is being very cheerful at somebody who is leaving in the morning.

3839432062.name: Hautdesert
3839432062.description: A castle where there should not be one, set in a clearing of pine with its moat frozen and every window lit. It looks cut out of paper against the snow.

lock.lockedText: The bower door is latched from the inside, and there is somebody moving about behind it. Not before you have been asked in.

npcs.name: Bertilak de Hautdesert
npcs.appearance: A great red-bearded man who laughs before the joke and stands too close while he does it.
npcs.persona: Enormously hospitable, and enjoying something you have not been told about yet.
knows: The Green Chapel is not two miles from his own gate.
He hunts every day of the feast and gives away everything he takes.
He proposes a game: what he wins in the wood he will give you, and what you win indoors you give him.

npcs.name: the Lady of Hautdesert
npcs.appearance: Very fair, very amused, and standing between you and the door on purpose.
npcs.persona: Tests people for sport and does not consider it unkind. Never quite says the thing outright.
knows: There is a green silk girdle in her bower that no man wearing it can be killed.
She would rather you took it than believed it.
Her lord's game is a game, and games have rules on both sides.

npcs.name: the porter of Hautdesert
npcs.appearance: Filling the gateway on purpose, with a staff he has not needed yet.
npcs.persona: Suspicious for exactly as long as it takes to hear your name, then embarrassing about it.
knows: Nobody has come up this road since the frost set in.
The gate stays barred at the feast, lord's orders, and the lord's orders are a joke he does not get.

npcs.name: an old woman
npcs.appearance: Wrapped to the eyes, very short, and watching you the whole time.
npcs.persona: Says almost nothing. What she does say has been thought about for a long while.
knows: She has been in this house longer than the lord has.
She asks whether you would rather be brave or alive, and does not accept both.

hooks: The lord hunts every day and gives away everything he catches, which is either generosity or a wager.
There is an old woman at the fire that the whole household defers to and nobody names.

3868645844.name: The Green Chapel
3868645844.description: Not a chapel. A green mound split open at one end, with a stream going under it and nothing on top but frozen grass. It is the ugliest holy place you have ever stood in front of.

npcs.name: the Green Knight
npcs.appearance: Green from beard to boot, and entirely undamaged about the neck.
npcs.persona: Cheerful, exact, and unhurried. Has been looking forward to this for a year.
knows: A blow for a blow, and the covenant was made in front of witnesses.
He knows precisely what you did and did not hand over at Hautdesert.
He is grinding the axe as you arrive, and takes his time about it.

hooks: Somebody is grinding a blade somewhere behind the mound, unhurriedly.

arc.title: A Blow for a Blow
arc.premise: A year ago you took the green man's head off in front of the whole court. Today you owe him the same courtesy, and the only question left is what you are willing to do to survive it.

quest.name: Take up the green axe
quest.description: It has hung in the keep at Camelot for a twelvemonth. Fetch it down; you are the one who has to return it.

beats.journal: Arthur will not tell me to stay. The axe the green man left is still in the keep, and it is mine to carry.

quest.name: Ride north to Hautdesert
quest.description: Out of the King's Hundred, over the water at Holm Ferry, and on into the pinewood until a roof shows. Hautdesert is the last one.

beats.journal: Kay says north: Holm Ferry, then the fen, then a lord's roof called Hautdesert. After that there is nothing to knock on.

quest.name: The mooring iron
quest.description: Somewhere in the reeds north of the Holm Ferry quay. Hodierne says she can hear the boats pulling at the stake all night.

beats.journal: Hodierne has lost the ferry's mooring iron in the reeds north of the quay. She knows this country; it is worth an hour.

quest.name: Ask the lord's leave
quest.description: The porter has let you into the courtyard. The lord of the house is somewhere in it, and it is his roof.

beats.journal: The gate of Hautdesert was barred against the feast. The porter has taken my name in and the bar is up.

quest.name: Keep the covenant
quest.description: Whatever you come by under this roof goes to the lord of it. Nothing kept back — that was the wording, and the hall heard it. His lady is in the bower off the hall, and the door is open now.

beats.journal: The lord's game: what he takes in the wood he gives me, and whatever I come by indoors I give him. His lady keeps the bower off the hall and I am asked in. He says the Green Chapel is two miles off and I may lie in bed until the day.

card.title: The covenant of the winnings
card.subtitle: sworn at the high table, with the hall listening

sections.heading: What he offers
sections.body: "I ride out at first light and you lie in, sir, for you have come a long way to be killed. And here is our game. Whatever I win in the wood is yours when I come home — and whatever you come by inside these walls, you hand over to me. Nothing kept back. Shall we swear it?"

sections.heading: What it costs
sections.body: It is a game the way a wager between friends is a game, and you have been in this house four hours. The whole hall drinks to it before you have finished agreeing.

quest.name: The green girdle
quest.description: A band of green silk in the Lady's Bower at Hautdesert, in the room she received you in. She says no man wearing it can be killed.

beats.journal: The lady says the green girdle is in her bower, within reach of the chair she sat me in, and that no man wearing it can be cut down. She said it lightly, which is worse.
I gave the lord the girdle with the rest of it. I go to the mound tomorrow with nothing on me but my own neck.

entry.text: I gave him the girdle with the rest of the day's winnings and said what it was. He went quiet for about as long as it takes to swallow, and then he was loud again.

beats.journal: I kept the girdle back. It is under my shirt and the lord has had everything else. Nothing kept back, was the wording.

entry.text: Three kisses handed over and one green girdle not. It is under my shirt. Nothing kept back was the wording, and I heard myself agree to it.

quest.name: Tell it at Camelot
quest.description: South by the fen road, the way you came. Arthur is in the hall and the account is owed to him — all of it, including the part you would rather leave out. Walk up to the king and say it.

beats.journal: He struck three times and I am alive. He has known where I have been every day of this, and who set it on.

card.title: The third blow
card.subtitle: at a green mound with a stream running under it

sections.heading: The first two
sections.body: He swings and stops. He swings and stops. "You flinched," he says the first time, pleasantly, the way you would tell a man his girth was loose. The second time he says nothing at all, and the second time you do not flinch.

sections.heading: The third
sections.body: The third comes down and takes the skin of your neck and no more of you than that, and the axe goes into the frozen ground beside your ear, and the green man leans on it and laughs until he has to stop and breathe.

beats.journal: The court heard it out and then laughed, and then every one of them put on a green band, and now it is a fashion and not a penance. That is the part I did not expect.

endings.title: The nick in the neck
endings.subtitle: a green belt, worn where everyone can see it

sections.heading: What the axe took
sections.body: Skin, and not much of that. He had two blows to give you for the two days you dealt straight with him, and both stopped short of your collar. The third was for the girdle you did not hand over, and it cost you the width of a thumbnail and the whole of your good opinion of yourself.

sections.heading: What you tell them
sections.body: You tell it at the high table, all of it, with the belt on the board in front of you, and you do not make yourself sound better than you were. Which is harder than kneeling was.

sections.heading: What they do with it
sections.body: They laugh. Not at you — at the shape of the thing, at a green man on a horse in a hall at Christmas, at the fact that you came back. Then every knight at that table ties a band of green silk on his arm, and by Easter it is a fashion and not a penance, and you are the only man in the kingdom still wearing his for the reason it was given.

sections.heading: What the axe took
sections.body: Nothing. Three times it came down and three times it stopped, and the third time he did not even mark you, because there was nothing left owing. You had handed him the girdle with the rest of the day's winnings and never told him what it was said to do, and he had known what it was said to do all along.

sections.heading: What he said after
sections.body: "There is no man walking who would have given that up," he said, leaning on the axe, "and I have looked. Go home, sir. There is nothing here worth your morning." He did not laugh. That was the part that stayed with you.

sections.heading: What you tell them
sections.body: The truth, and it makes a poor tale: a man kept a promise and lived. The court wants a wound out of it and there is not one to show. So it goes into the books thin, and every knight at that table quietly decides he would have done the same, and not one of them is sure.

endings.title: The road back
endings.subtitle: with the axe still on your saddle

sections.heading: The covenant
sections.body: You went north in the frost, and you found the mound, and you knelt in front of a man who should not have had a head to speak with. Whatever else is written down, that part is settled.

sections.heading: And now
sections.body: The road south is the same road. It only feels shorter because you know how it ends.

entry.text: The Green Axe is heavier than a year of remembering it made it. Nobody in the hall watched me take it down, which took some arranging on their part.
The ferry is tied to a stake because the mooring iron went into the reeds. The woman who works it knows this country better than anyone I have met on the road.

The Green Chapel is a grass mound with a hole at either end and a stream going under it, and there is a noise coming out of it like a scythe on a wheel. It goes further under the hill than anyone has been.

barriers.lockedText: The gate of Hautdesert is barred across the whole arch, and there is a man behind it who has not decided about you yet.
barriers.opensText: The bar goes up, both leaves swing in, and the warmth comes out at you like a hand.

item.name: Green Axe
item.description: Head the length of a forearm, haft wound with green, and not a spot of rust on it in a twelvemonth.

placements.emptyText: The bracket it hung on is still there, and the wall behind it is a shade darker than the rest.

item.name: Green Girdle
item.description: A band of green silk hemmed in gold thread. Light as nothing, and warm, which it should not be.

placements.emptyText: Folded linen, a comb, and the shape in the pile where something used to sit.

item.name: Mooring Iron
item.description: Two feet of pitted ring-iron, weighing about what a bad decision weighs.

placements.emptyText: Black water closing over the print your hand left in the silt.

item.name: Holly Bob
item.description: A bough of holly, still green, still berried, cut this morning by somebody who was not in a hurry.

placements.emptyText: Berries on the rock, and the wet ring where the bough was standing.

item.name: Green Whetstone
item.description: A wheel of green stone worn hollow on one side, still wet, with a smell of iron about it.

placements.emptyText: A ring of wet on the rock where it was standing, and the drip going on somewhere further in.

hall.speech: Eleven days of feast and not one of us has said the word. Very well: I shall not say it either. The axe is in the keep, nephew, where it has hung since he carried his own head out of that door.

choices.text: Say the word and I will stay.
Where in the keep? It is a deep house.
Then I will fetch it down.

refuse.speech: I will not. A king who calls a man back from a covenant made at this table has no table. Ask me for anything else and it is yours before you finish asking.

choices.text: Then the axe, and your blessing.
Where in the keep is it?

keep.speech: Ground floor, in the stores along the north side — a green haft standing out of a barrel among four that hold nothing but salt. Look in the barrels, nephew. Nobody has wanted to touch it, so nobody has moved it either.

choices.text: Then I will go and look.

north.speech: North. There is a road as far as Holm Ferry and after the water there is a track, and after the track there is the waste. One roof out there keeps Christmas — Hautdesert. Knock loudly and give your own name; they bar the gate at the feast and the porter is not a reader of faces.

choices.text: Where in the keep is the axe?

chapel.speech: Nobody at this table has seen it. Nobody at this table saw a man pick his own head off my floor either, and I have that written down as well. Ask at Hautdesert — a lord who lives in the waste knows what is in it.

bless.speech: Take it, then. And take this, which is the only argument I have left: the shield is painted with the five joys and the five virtues, and every one of them holds or none of them do. Go by the north gate. Kay is in it, being unbearable, and he has your road written down.

choices.text: Where in the keep is the axe?

actions.description: Red, with a five-pointed knot in gold. Every line of it goes through every other.

again.speech: Still here. Good. The axe is still in the keep — north side, in the barrels — and I am still not going to say it.

returned.speech: You are standing in my hall with a scar and a green rag, and you have told it as though it were a confession. Nephew. Look behind you.

choices.text: I would rather they did not.

fashion.speech: Every man at this table has tied a green band on his arm, and by Easter it will mean nothing at all and they will still be wearing it. That is what a court does with a thing like this. Let it.

returned-clean.speech: You are standing in my hall without a mark on you, nephew, and you have told it as though you were apologising for it. A man rode north at Christmas to be killed, and came back whole because he kept his word and would not be bought out of it. Look behind you.

choices.text: There is no wound to show them.
I only did what I said I would.
He gave me nothing to carry home.

fashion-clean.speech: Every man at this table has tied a green band on his arm, and not one of them could tell you what it stands for, because there is no wound in it and no wound is a poor song. Let them wear it. You and I know what it cost to come back with nothing to show, and that is the whole of the account and the best of it.

gate.speech: Ah. The condemned. Your horse is shod, your girth is new and I have had your cloak relined, none of which you asked for, so do not thank me for it in front of anyone.

choices.text: You do not believe in it.

road.speech: North out of the meadow and keep the water on your left as far as Holm Ferry. Past the ferry it is fen and pinewood and it stays fen and pinewood for a day. There is one roof out there and it is called Hautdesert. Bar's down at the feast, so knock and give your name — your whole name.

ferry.speech: A woman called Hodierne, three roofs and more boats than hands. She has worked that channel thirty years and she has lost the mooring iron in the reeds north of her own quay, which she will tell you about at length. Help her and she will tell you what is north of her, which nobody else can.

choices.text: I have no time for lost ironmongery.

doubt.speech: I believe in a man in green paint and a trick with a head, and I believe you have ridden out for it, and I am not able to say which of those annoys me more. Go on. Go before I have to be sincere.

gate-again.speech: Still in the gateway. So are you, which is worse. North, past Holm Ferry, and knock at Hautdesert with your own name in your mouth.

chapel.speech: You have come to be told it does not count. It counts. A promise made in a hall in front of witnesses is a promise, and the witnesses are the part that binds, not the hall.

choices.text: Then tell me how to keep it.
I came for a blessing, not a lecture.

five.speech: Generosity, courtesy, chastity, fellowship, piety. Five, and each of them holds the other four up — which is the whole of the pentangle and the whole of the difficulty. A man does not fail at one of them. He fails at one and finds he has failed at five.

choices.text: That is a hard shield to carry.
I will try to carry it.

how.speech: Truthfully. If you are offered something out there that will keep you alive, take it or refuse it as you see fit — but do not take it and say you did not. That is the only way this goes badly.

chapel-again.speech: Still counting, sir. It still counts.

quay.speech: You are the fourth thing to come up that road this winter and the other three were geese. Over the water, is it? It will cost you nothing today; I cannot moor properly and I will not take payment for a bad job.

choices.text: What is wrong with the mooring?
Have you seen a green man?

iron.speech: The iron went off the quay-end into the reeds in the dark. North of here, fifteen paces past the last shed, where the ground stops being ground — look in the reeds themselves, not the open water. Bring it back and I will tell you what you are riding into, which is worth more than the fare.

choices.text: North, in the reeds. I will look.
Have you seen a green man?

north.speech: Pines, and then a lord's roof, and then a mound out east past the pines that the fowlers walk round rather than over. Something rings out there at first light like a smith at work, and there is no smith. That is all I will say for free.

choices.text: Tell me about the mooring iron.

green.speech: Green paint I have seen. Green *skin* I have not, and I have been asked that twice this year, which is twice more than in the thirty before it. Somebody is putting it about, sir. Somebody wants it known.

asking.speech: A pedlar in the autumn, and a woman off the fen road who did not buy anything. Small, old, wrapped to the eyes. She asked whether the road to Camelot was open and then went back the way she came.

iron-back.speech: You went into the reeds for it. Well. Then here is the fare back and a word with it: at the mound, whatever is said to you, it will be true. That is the trouble with it out there. Nothing lies.

choices.text: Nothing lies. I will remember it.
Who has been asking about green men?

actions.description: A twist of green withy and a coin, tied the way the ferry folk tie them. It has been in the water.

quay-again.speech: Still on my quay. The reeds are still north of it, and the iron is still in them.

iron-thanks.speech: The boats are on the iron again and they have stopped complaining about it, which is more than the men do. You have the fare whenever you want it, and the fen charm — keep that where you can reach it.

choices.text: Who has been asking about green men?

barred.speech: Stand off the gate. Nothing has come up this road since the frost and I am not opening to a horse I cannot see the colour of. Name yourself and be quick, it is perishing.

choices.text: Gawain of Arthur's house, and I am freezing.
A man looking for the Green Chapel.

whose.speech: Bertilak's. And before you ask — yes, in the middle of the waste, and yes, we keep the feast, and yes, everyone says it. Name, sir.

choices.text: A man looking for the Green Chapel.

name.speech: Gawain. Of Arthur's — right. Right. Well. My lord will have the gate off its hinges if I keep you out there, and I will hear about it at supper for a year. Bar's up. He is in the courtyard; you cannot miss him, he is the loudest thing in the waste.

chapel.speech: Everybody out here is looking for the Green Chapel and none of them look twice. Give me a name, sir, or give me the road back.

choices.text: Then I will take the road back.

barred-again.speech: Bar's up, sir, and I have had my ear bent about it twice already. The lord is in the court.

welcome.speech: Gawain! In my house, at my feast, in the one week of the year I would have asked for you. Whatever you have ridden here for can wait until you have eaten. It can, sir. I insist on it.

choices.text: I am looking for a green chapel.
You are very glad to see me.
Who else is under this roof?

household.speech: My lady, who will find you out inside an hour, and an old woman by the fire who has been here longer than I have and is nobody's business but her own. And thirty men who hunt. Now — the chapel.

choices.text: The old woman. Who is she?

old-woman.speech: Ha. Ask her. I have known her twenty years and I could not tell you her name if you held the axe to me. She sits by the fire, she says very little, and what she says has been thought about.

two-miles.speech: Then you are the luckiest man in the waste, because it is not two miles from this gate — east, past the pines, a green mound with a stream going under it — and I will send a lad to walk you there on the day. Which leaves you three days in a warm hall with nothing to do. So: a game.

choices.text: I have had my fill of games in halls.

certain.speech: I have hunted every yard of it since I was nine. East until the trees stop, and it is the only hill with a hole in either end of it. You will hear it before you see it — there is a wheel turning down in the dark of it most mornings. Now. A game.

covenant.speech: I ride out at dawn and you lie in. Whatever I win in the wood, I give to you. And whatever you come by inside these walls, you give to me. Nothing kept back. Swear it and drink.

choices.text: And if I come by nothing?
Nothing kept back is a wide net, my lord.

nothing.speech: Then you give me nothing, and I am out a deer, and my lady will say I was cheated. It is wide because a narrow one would not be a game. Swear it.

sworn.speech: Sworn! Drink. My lady keeps the bower off the hall and the door is open to you — she will keep you company while I am out in the cold like a fool, and I am the fool who arranged it.

bower-way.speech: Off the hall, the small house with the shutters painted. It is open. Knock or do not; she will have heard you cross the yard either way.

third-day.speech: The third day, and the third of the hunt: a fox, and a poor one, and it is yours. Now. What have you come by under my roof, sir? Nothing kept back — that was the wording, and the hall heard it.

choices.text: Take this. It is all I have won here.
Three kisses and no more than that.
Nothing of hers is on me. Ask me tomorrow.

given.speech: Green silk. Hers, unless I have gone blind as well as red. Well. That is honestly done, sir, and it is more than I looked for, and I shall say so at a better time than this one. Sleep. The lad will have you at the mound by first light.

withheld.speech: Three kisses, and I get a fox for them. Ha! There is no justice under this roof and I built it myself. Sleep, sir. The lad will have you at the mound by first light.

lord-again.speech: Eat something, sir. You are going to a mound in the morning — east, past the pines — and you will want the weight on you.

bower.speech: The door was open, and you knocked at it anyway. Sit down, sir — no, there, by the fire, you have been cold for four days. My lord is out killing something and I have been very much looking forward to being disappointing to you.

choices.text: My lady, I am your lord's guest.
What do you know about the mound?

mound.speech: That it is old, that it is not a chapel, and that men who go to it come back changed or do not come back. And that my lord speaks of it as one speaks of a field one owns. Make of that what you like; I have been making something of it for years.

choices.text: You think he knows more than he says.
Then how does a man survive it?

guest.speech: You are, and you will keep saying it, and I shall keep enjoying it. Very well. If you will not take anything of mine for love, take one thing for sense. There is a green girdle in this room, sir, within arm's reach of where you are sitting. No man who wears it can be cut down.

choices.text: I cannot take your lord's goods.
Why give it to me at all?

why.speech: Because I would rather you lived, and because I would rather know what you do about it. Both are true and you may weigh them however you please.

sense.speech: It costs you a conversation with him you would rather not have. That is the whole of the price, and you are the one who decides whether it is dear. Look at it, at least — it is in the room with you. It is only silk until you want it.

choices.text: Why give it to me at all?

bower-again.speech: Still here, still courteous. It is still in this room, sir, and my lord is still out in the cold.

choices.text: What do you know about the mound?

fire.speech: Sit where I can see you. There. — No, I am not going to say anything useful. I am very old and I am warm and you are the most interesting thing to come through that gate in nine years.

choices.text: Then let me ask you something.
I will leave you to the fire.

met.speech: We have not. But I knew your mother, and I knew her sister, and one of those two would be very pleased to see you sitting here. I shall not tell you which.

choices.text: Then let me ask you something else.

ask.speech: Ask, then. Would you rather be brave, or alive? — and do not say both. Both is what men say when they have not yet been offered the choice, and you are going to be offered it before Thursday.

choices.text: Both, and I know what you will say.

brave.speech: Good. That is the right answer and it is very easy to give in a warm room. Remember that you gave it. Somebody will remind you if you do not.

alive.speech: Honest, at least. Most men lie to me about that and every one of them takes the belt anyway.

choices.text: I did not say I would take anything.

belt.speech: Nothing. An old woman by a fire. Go and be courteous at somebody.

fire-again.speech: Still warm. Still old. Still watching you, sir.

choices.text: Would I rather be brave or alive?

not-yet.speech: Early, sir. I am not ready and neither are you — look at your hands, there is nothing in them. You have a night left under that man's roof and an account to render him before you have any business kneeling here. Whatever his lady has put in your way, settle it with him, and then come back and I will be as quick as I know how.

choices.text: What is down under the hill?

account.speech: You swore a game with him: what he takes in the wood is yours, and what you come by under his roof is his. Nothing kept back — you said it in front of his whole hall and I heard about it before the cups were down. Go and keep it, or do not keep it. Either way I want you standing here knowing which you did.

choices.text: What is down under the hill?

mound.speech: You came. Do you know, I said you would, and there was money against it in that house. Kneel down, sir, and hold still, and we will have this over before the light is properly up.

choices.text: There was money against it in what house?

house.speech: You will work it out in about four minutes and I would not spoil it. Kneel down.

chapel.speech: It is the only one out here and nobody consecrated it, which suits both of us. It goes further under the hill than you would care to walk, and I keep my wheel down at the bottom of it — you have been listening to it since first light. Kneel down.

down.speech: Water, mostly. Cold, a long way in, and a green stone I have worn hollow on one side. Take it afterwards if you have the legs for it — you will have earned a souvenir.

strike.speech: Three at your neck and one of them home, and that is the whole of it. I have been the man in the wood, and the man in the hall, and the lady's errand too, and I have watched you every day of this. You were true twice. The third time you loved your life a little, and God knows I do not blame you.

choices.text: You were the lord of that house.

morgan.speech: An old woman by my fire that you walked past four times. She wanted a court frightened and she got one man cut, which is the usual exchange rate for a plan like that. Take the belt. Wear it or do not.

verdict.speech: Failed! You are the truest man that ever walked, sir — you are simply not the perfect one, and nobody told you there was a difference. Go home. South by the fen road, the way you came. Tell it as it happened. That is the last of the covenant and it is the hard half.

choices.text: I will tell it as it happened.
What is down under the hill?

mound-again.speech: Go home, sir. South by the fen road. There is nothing else out here and I have a house to get back to.

choices.text: What is down under the hill?

strike-clean.speech: Three at your neck, and not one of them touched you. There it is. I have been the man in the wood, and the man in the hall, and the lady's errand besides, and I have watched you every day of this. You handed her belt over with the rest of the day's winnings and never once said what it was for. Do you know how few men get that far?

choices.text: You were the lord of that house.

morgan-clean.speech: An old woman by my fire that you walked past four times. She wanted a court frightened, and what she has got is one knight who could not be bought with his own life, which is a poor return on the trouble she went to. Take the belt back. You had it, and you gave it up; nobody can take that off you twice.

verdict-clean.speech: There is no man walking who would have given that up, sir, and I have looked. Not one blow owing and not a mark on you to prove any of it — which you will find is the hardest kind of story to tell, and you are going to have to tell it anyway. Go home. South by the fen road. Say it as it happened and let the court make what it can of a man who simply kept his word.

choices.text: I will tell it as it happened.
What is down under the hill?
